messages.subject: Windows: Building models
parts:
We were able to compile the multivariate distributions under windows
by giving cc1plus.exe (part of gcc) more stack space. To do this:
1) Open a command window.
2) Set up the command window to have access to MSDN tools
- Run: >"C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio
10.0\VC\vcvarsall.bat"
3) Find the location of cc1plus.exe and change to that directory:
- Run: > gcc --print-prog-name cc1plus
- change directory to the location of the executable
3) See how much stack space is available in cc1plus.exe.
- Run: > dumpbin /HEADERS cc1plus.exe
4) Edit the stack space
- Run: > editbin /STACK:10000000 cc1plus.exe

That allows us to run the matrix unit tests and run models. At this
moment, we still have issues building the compiler, stanc. It looks
like a problem with the gnu assembler.

Daniel

> Do we have a theory as to why Windows requires much more stack space for these multivariate things than !Windows?

Why Windows specifically, I don't know.

Nor do we have any idea why the GNU assembler craps
out on Windows.

But template metaprograms are notorious consumers
of compiler stack because they're programmed
recursively. It was dying in Eigen, which certainly
indicates template metaprograms as the culprit.

Our templating for auto-dif or auto return type calcs
or static conditionals are relatively easy on the
compiler compared to Eigen's use of all that plus
expression templates.

- Bob

and then calling with integers.

int literals.

generator to static cast all the int values to
double values -- I have all that information at the
code-generation point because I have to do type-checking
with integer promotion to double.

100K prior for variance looks really arbitrary
when it's square-rooted to 316!

want to do the forward part of the model.
